input_text: On the issue of whether Susan was familiar with Shakespeare, the fact that she had once played the role of Macbeth and recieved a standing ovation after her monologue.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The evidence is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted—specifically, that Susan was familiar with Shakespeare. This satisfies the 'offered to prove the truth' prong of the hearsay definition.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) hearsay definition requires the statement be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Susan was familiar with Shakespeare

arguments.text: The proffered evidence consists of Susan's conduct (playing the role of Macbeth and receiving a standing ovation), which is non-assertive conduct rather than a declarative statement. Under FRE 801(a), conduct is not a statement unless intended as such, and here it serves as circumstantial evidence.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a 'statement' as a written/oral assertion or nonverbal conduct intended as an assertion. Non-assertive conduct is not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that she had once played the role of Macbeth and recieved a standing ovation after her monologue.

arguments.text: The narrative contains no indication that Susan made an out-of-court assertion regarding her familiarity with Shakespeare. Without an assertion, the hearsay rule under FRE 801(c) is not triggered.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires an out-of-court assertion to constitute hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that she had once played the role of Macbeth and recieved a standing ovation after her monologue.

arguments.text: The evidence is purely circumstantial in nature, relying on the inference that playing Macbeth implies familiarity with Shakespeare. Pure circumstantial evidence that does not depend on an out-of-court assertion is not hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: Circumstantial evidence is distinguishable from hearsay; hearsay requires a statement, whereas circumstantial evidence relies on logical inference from conduct.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that she had once played the role of Macbeth and recieved a standing ovation after her monologue.
